caution_points.item: If the school is public, then it is considered more prestigious than a private school
Short code bootcamps do not necessarily indicate great expertise in coding
Be careful not to confuse an online course with actually studying at the school
Having worked at a prestigious consulting firm indicates strong analytical skills
Participating in student associations indicates a good level of communication and soft skills
Having been promoted within one's company indicates a good overall level and strong work capacity
A salesperson who has been an SDR will be able to effectively manage SDRs in a managerial role
A tech person who mentions all technologies will likely have very little expertise in each of them
A developer who mentions a technology with a spelling mistake is a sign that they may not have a good grasp of it
If the candidate is a member of a professional club (HR lab, growth club...), then they are likely good at their job
The larger the clients of the company, the longer and more complex the sales processes are
The presence of emojis on the profile is an indicator of good soft skills
Staying in a company for a long time is an indicator of seriousness and commitment, but staying too long can be an indicator of a lack of adventure and challenge
Having worked in a renowned company in the tech/sales/marketing field is highly valued
In companies operating in multiple countries and/or with their headquarters abroad, it is likely that English is the working language
In France, a BBA is less prestigious than a master's degree, even in a good school
In France, an enginner must be issued from a school recognized by the Comission sur les Titres d'Ingénieur (CTI) to be considered as such.
In France, an enginner is most of the time generalist, so it's similar to a master's degree in all fields related to engineering (mechanical, electrical, civil, computer science etc.)
